title: Station restrictions and special operations
blurb: Define spurious emissions and know who your station must protect, what PRB-1 requires, and how RACES works.

E1B01.why: Spurious emissions are energy **outside the necessary bandwidth** that you can reduce or remove without harming the message.
E1B01.trap: A specific dB figure or an ID problem is not the definition.

E1B02.why: Digital voice and slow-scan TV on HF stay within about **3 kHz**, roughly one voice channel. The larger choices are too wide.

E1B03.why: Protect an FCC monitoring facility from harmful interference within **1 mile**.

E1B04.why: If a radiolocation system suffers interference from your 70 cm repeater, the control operator must **cease operation or mitigate** the interference.
E1B04.trap: The rule names no NOTAM filing or antenna-height cut, so "all of these" is wrong.

E1B05.why: The National Radio Quiet Zone surrounds the **National Radio Astronomy Observatory**.

E1B06.why: Near a public use airport you **may have to notify the FAA** and register the structure with the FCC under **Part 17**.

E1B07.why: PRB-1 applies to **state and local zoning** regulations.
E1B07.trap: PRB-1 covers government zoning, not private covenants or FAA height limits.

E1B08.why: With good receivers, the FCC can require the station to **avoid certain hours** on the frequencies that cause the interference. It is not a full shutdown.
E1B08.trap: Cease-all-operation and below or above 30 MHz bans are too broad.

E1B09.why: Any licensed amateur station **certified by the responsible civil defense organization** for the area it serves may operate under RACES.

E1B10.why: RACES stations may use **all amateur frequencies authorized to the control operator**. No special segments or government channels.

E1B11.why: PRB-1 requires **reasonable accommodation** of amateur radio, not a ban and not an absolute right.
